buildInPublic.direction: Operate within the incumbent FlowSight mobile family

navigation.outer: Online contains Leagues and Build in public
navigation.selection: Card-colored selected outer tab; four studio views immediately beneath it with an 18px gap, 36px minimum-height controls and 2px teal underline; returned-content count beside Content. The feature h1 remains accessible but is visually hidden.

buildInPublic.layout: Compact two-column period/generation toolbar with a 9px gap; optional text direction behind a disclosure; title-first current ideas, retained earlier ideas and saved selections remain distinguishable. Selected count and Prepare prompts open a dedicated inline setup step.
buildInPublic.responsive: Studio width caps at 760px and optional portrait preview at 360px from 700px. Idea rows use the studio width. Setup style/profile fields stack in compact windows and use two equal columns from 560px. Content padding is 12px top and 40px bottom; at heights up to 550px, top padding is 8px and toolbar controls reduce from 38px to 34px minimum height. Outer tabs stay at 34px minimum height.

storyChoice.structure: Separate checkbox and text column; date and confirmation beneath title; independent Review action

focus.continuity: Same-view renders restore the active control and text selection; view navigation moves to a heading; editor fallback is the back control; the live-region node persists

buildInPublic.evidence: A successful batch supplies five editorial alternatives grounded in local observations. Current and earlier batches stay local until a reviewed highlight is explicitly saved. Saved selections have a separate heading/count and a Review action.
buildInPublic.prompts: Subject-first divided rows show network, style and returned-content status. The editor preserves the complete stored prompt, shows unsaved changes and exposes explicit Save, Copy and Delete actions.
buildInPublic.profiles: Social profiles are stored independently in FlowSight with network, name, handle and usual style; they supply prompt context without a Buffer account requirement.
buildInPublic.assistant: Scoped revocable MCP connection exposes get_content_context, set_content_direction and save_content_drafts. The assistant can guide the next five-idea local selection and return proposals. Any later publication is handled outside FlowSight.
buildInPublic.returnedContent: Subject-first divided rows show network/state, a two-line body preview, origin and revision. The editor separates post or first message from full thread, script or slide plan, with an optional visual outline. Save, Copy and Delete actions are available; approval, schedule, destination and publication controls are absent.
buildInPublic.errorRecovery: Profile, preference and direction form drafts survive busy/error renders and clear after successful writes or an owner change. Stable local identities retain current/earlier ideas and corrections across generation; unfinished manual highlights are cached locally. Evidence, prompt and proposal edits survive ordinary internal navigation with unsaved status visible. Draft retention does not upload evidence.
buildInPublic.incomingContent: A minute-based studio check refreshes returned content, its count and assistant-set text direction in an idle open view, including manual idea cadence. Active editors, focused forms and ongoing requests defer refresh; the existing live region reports updates without stealing focus.

narrative.overview:
The desktop renderer belongs to the FlowSight mobile family. A pale technical grid, slate reading text, teal signals, softly raised white panels, and one indigo-to-teal tracking action make the compact Tauri window feel related to the Android app without stretching a phone screen into desktop proportions.

The visual language carries through Today, Insights, Settings, first run, and consent. It puts a clear tracking decision beside measured time, then uses quieter cards and rails for supporting evidence. This contract describes the desktop WebView and its shared interface patterns.

Onboarding and session planning follow the Operate direction within this incumbent family: compact labelled controls, useful examples, visible progress and status, and an explicit primary action at each decision. Their dark teal actions support white labels while the existing lighter teal continues to carry state and progress.

Build in public extends this Operate direction inside Online. It keeps the gridded ground and compact type, with labelled choices, open rows, and quiet separators. Clear evidence, editable prompts, and returned proposals share the same working surface and retain their distinct meanings.
keyCharacteristics: A 56px pale grid behind centered, softly layered work surfaces.
Manrope for headings and measured display figures; Plus Jakarta Sans for reading and controls.
Teal for state and progress, with an indigo-to-teal gradient concentrated in tracking and first-run actions.
A floating five-control dock that stays available in the narrow work window.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Use teal to show state, progress, selection, or a real action. Concentrate the indigo-to-teal gradient on tracking and first-run decisions.

rules.name: The Measurement Rule
rules.body: Keep numbers aligned with tabular numerals while preserving the same Manrope display voice as the rest of the interface.

rules.name: The Subject First Rule
rules.body: In Build in public lists, lead with the useful idea title. Keep the source excerpt, recorded signals, network, and status subordinate to that subject.

rules.name: The Layer Rule
rules.body: Give ordinary content a quiet lift; reserve the stronger shadow for persistent navigation and blocking overlays.

dos: Do use the 56px grid as a quiet background behind readable surfaces.
Do keep Manrope display type and Plus Jakarta Sans reading type together across tabs.
Do use the indigo-to-teal gradient for tracking and first-run primary actions, with solid teal for routine confirmations.
Do keep the dock and consent actions reachable in narrow, short windows.
donts: Don't stretch the phone layout or its spacing directly into a wide desktop window.
Don't use teal on every card or turn observed activity into a score-like visual.
Don't let the floating dock cover the last controls in a scrolled pane.
Don't hide remaining consent details behind a fixed action row without a visible way to reach them.
